_help: HOW TO ADD DIALOGUE: append an entry to 'sequences'. Each sequence has an id, a trigger and a list of lines.
cards_left / cards_drawn count the draw pile (deck); cards_drawn counts from when the dealer finishes dealing. A sequence plays once and sequences that trigger together are queued.
A 'manual' sequence never starts by itself; include it from another sequence with a line like { "play_sequence": "shuffle" }.
Line fields: speaker (a DialogueSpeaker speaker_id, or 'player' for internal thoughts), text, and optionally
audio (res:// path to a clip; it plays from the speaker and sets the line length), delay (seconds before the line),
duration (override the line length), pause (seconds after the line). Without audio the length is estimated from the text.

event (runs a table action when the line starts: 'shuffle_deck', 'deal_hands', 'wait_for_drain', 'collect_and_deal', 'start_final_phase', 'wait_for_game_end', 'begin_ending', 'ending_cards_to_candle', 'ending_burn', 'ending_open_door' or 'ending_fade_out'); add "wait": true to hold the line until it finishes.
A line with no text is a silent step: { "event": "wait_for_drain", "wait": true } runs the action and waits for it; { "wait": true } just waits for any action still running.

Sequence options: "disable_play": true stops all players (including you) from playing cards while that sequence runs. "interrupt": true makes it start right after the current line of whatever is playing (which then resumes).
Trigger option: "round": 1 or 2 only lets a cards_left trigger fire in that round (round 2 starts once the dealer has collected the final pile and dealt everyone back up to five).

Ending: 'begin_ending' (scripts/ending_sequence.gd) queues, if unmatched cards remain, ending_win_<speaker_id> for the player with the most sets (ties go to the dealer), then ending_question_<left_npc|right_npc> and ending_burn. If every card is matched it queues ending_matched (the door opens; the knight's first line waits 8 s via its delay so the door is already swinging).

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Well, I guess I start since I'm the dealer.

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: Why did they choose you to be the dealer anyway?

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Probably because I'm the worst criminal here.

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: Ha. Don't flatter yourself.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Five cards in hand, no more. Make a set and it goes face up on the table. No arguing.

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: And when the deck runs out?

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: I reshuffle. Once. Same as they told us.

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: They told us the rules a dozen times.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I can't afford to lose. I'm not dying tonight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I should probably be careful that they're not watching when I peek at their cards.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Hold on, let me shuffle.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: The first round must come to an end. Everybody make sure your discard pile is empty.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Then we wait until every card has made it to the final pile: the left's discard.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: So I keep discarding until every pile runs dry.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: That's all of them. I'll collect the final pile, shuffle it, and deal everyone back up to five.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Round two. This deck is the last one, so make it count.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Last chance. Whoever has the most sets walks out of here.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: That's the last card. Make your final sets, then discard whatever you have left.

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: And then what happens?

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Nobody told me that part.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Nobody told any of us that part.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: As expected, I won.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: To my dismay, Flynn won.

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: Ha ha, see ya losers!

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Congrats, Melanie.

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: I'm free!

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Seems like you have the most sets.

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: So what happens now?

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: So what happens now?

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Are all cards matched?

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: Yeah, what's the big deal?

lines.speaker: knight
lines.text: You are all free to go...

lines.speaker: knight
lines.text: ...except you. I saw what you did, and I'll admit, I'm impressed...

lines.speaker: knight
lines.text: ...but it's not supposed to work that way either.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: We will get rid of the stragglers efficiently.

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: Wait, it's not supposed to work this way!

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: You ever wonder who's paying for all this? The candles, the wine, a whole room just for us.

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: The state. The same people who put us here.

lines.speaker: dealer
lines.text: Rehabilitation through competition. That's what the paperwork called it.

lines.speaker: left_npc
lines.text: I signed mine without reading it. Didn't think anyone read those.

lines.speaker: right_npc
lines.text: Eyes on your own cards, all of you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Nobody here is going to play fair. I shouldn't either.
